newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds recoup losses but future uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds recoup losses but future uncertain.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds recouped Thursday's losses in early trade on Friday, with a U.S. rate rise next Tuesday already factored into the market but players waiting for confirmation before the next move, traders said.

"The market has already discounted a 25 point rate increase and, if it is confirmed on Tuesday, we could rally again," one trader said. "The only problem will be if he (U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan) makes it a 50 point rise."
"Although that is only an outside chance, people are being cautious and will wait before getting into the market again," the trader added.
Traders said an added element of uncertainty was Monday's Belgian bond auction.
ABN-AMRO said in its morning market commentary it did not expect the Treasury to offer much of OLOs 25 (March 2001) and 26 (March 2007) at the auction.
Added to this is the quantity of coupons coming to maturity on March 28.
Traders estimated the value at between 40 and 50 billion Belgian francs.
"I expect most of this to come back into the market which will provide good support," one trader said.
"If it doesn't come back it will be bad for bonds, but I expect it to. It essentially has nowhere else to go," he added. "We will see on Tuesday."
At 1000 GMT the yield of the benchmark March 2007 OLO was 6.04 percent against Thursday's closing 6.11, and the spread over German Bunds was 15 basis points against 16.
The March futures contract was 45 basis points higher at 120.40.
